name: MathlibAnnex.lexicographicRefine
title: Successive maximum refinement by an ordered list of functionals

content.display_title: Successive maximum refinement by an ordered list of functionals
content.one_sentence_role: Defines a nonempty compact set of survivors after maximizing finitely many functionals in order.
content.natural_language_statement: For a nonempty compact set $K$ in a real normed space and a finite ordered list $\boldsymbol\ell=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r)$ of continuous linear functionals, successively retain the points maximizing $\ell_1$, then those maximizing $\ell_2$ on the retained set, and so on. The resulting set is denoted $\mathcal R_{\boldsymbol\ell}(K)$.
content.definition_explanation:
Let $K_\ell=\{x\in K:\ell(x)=\max_{y\in K}\ell(y)\}$. The complete recursion is

$$\mathcal R_{()}(K)=K,\qquad\mathcal R_{(\ell,\boldsymbol\eta)}(K)=\mathcal R_{\boldsymbol\eta}(K_\ell).$$

The maximum of each later functional is taken on the current retained set. Changing the order can therefore change the resulting set.
content.assumptions: The ambient space is any real normed vector space. The set $K$ is nonempty and compact, and the list is finite and ordered. No finite-dimensionality or point-separation assumption is needed for this definition.
content.conclusion: The result is a nonempty compact set. For the empty list it is $K$ itself. A singleton conclusion requires a separate point-separation hypothesis; this definition does not select a single point.
content.lean_realization_notes: Each maximum slice is nonempty compact by continuity on a nonempty compact set. Thus every recursive step is defined. Later lemmas show that the final set lies in $K$ and that all survivors have the same value under every functional in the list. If the list separates points, those equalities force the final set to be a singleton.
